text:
sam: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selector tweak I see a consistent p99 bump (about +18%) on the customer perf-runner tests that have high prefix cache hit ratios. Thought it might be a kernel perf regression, but the flamegraphs point at batching behaviour.

rita: Hmm. do you have the chain of events? cache hit ratio high => shorter active token budgets => batch formation changed?

sam: Exactly. Example trace: 
```
request A: prefix_hit=true, gen_tokens=6
request B: prefix_hit=false, gen_tokens=48
request C: prefix_hit=true, gen_tokens=4
```
With the current continuous-batcher we use a fixed token_budget_target=128 and greedily pack. High ratio of tiny requests is causing many mixed batches where the cold (miss) requests are delayed waiting for more tokens to reach target. p50 good but p99 for cold requests spikes.

devin: That matches the simulation we ran in Aug — if avg tokens per req drops, the queue waits longer to fill target, wasting tail latency. Did the selector change alter kernel throughput per-token?

sam: selector change improved cold single-request throughput by ~6% but changed latency variance for mixed batches. So kernel change didn't cause a regression alone, but increased sensitivity of the batching heuristic to request mix.

rita: Proposed mitigation: two ideas — 1) dynamic token_budget_target based on moving window of recent token per-request distribution (so burst of small requests reduces target), or 2) slotting: reserve N token-slots per batch for cold (miss) requests so misses don't starve.

tom: +1 for slotting. We've seen starvation before. But slotting config needs to be simple or ops will misconfigure. Maybe an adaptive slot count: slot_count = clamp( floor(total_budget * cold_frac / avg_cold_tokens), 1, max_slots ).

devin: Another thought: dual-queue admission. Keep hot-queue (prefix hits) and cold-queue. Batches are formed by pulling up to K cold requests first (to satisfy latency SLOs), then fill with hot requests up to the budget. This preserves batching efficiency but prioritizes misses.

sam: I prototyped that overnight. Config snippet: 
```
batch_config:
  total_budget: 128
  max_slots_for_cold: 8
  cold_priority_quota: 0.25   # at least 25% of tokens must be cold
  adapt_window_secs: 10
  min_cold_slots: 1
```
Behavior: if cold_frac drops, cold_priority_quota decays, freeing more room to hot.

rita: Nice. Any perf numbers from the prototype?

sam: Quick run on perf-runner: cold p99 down from +18% back to baseline +2%. cold p50 unchanged. Hot p50 slightly worse (~+3%) but within SLO. Overall token utilization unchanged.

perf-bot: [profile-attached] quick diff: slotting-mode vs baseline -> cold tail improved, hot median regressed ~2.7%, overall throughput steady.

tom: What about kernel selection interplay? If kernels vary per seq-len, the hot (short seq) dominated batches may now pick different kernel and reduce per-token cost — but mixed batches could cause kernel-switch overhead. Do we need to group by kernel fingerprint as well?

devin: Good point. We should prefer homogeneous-kernel packing when possible. Heuristic: when forming a batch, prefer same kernel family (fp16-quant or int8) as the current head-of-queue; but allow cross-kernel if cold quota requires it.

sam: That helped in microbenchmarks. Implementation detail: we compute a kernel_score for candidate requests and reject inclusion if score delta > threshold unless forced by cold slots. Avoids runtime kernel-state churn.

rita: Ops safety: we need a telemetry flag and rollout plan. Suggest rollout in three stages: 1) simulated-mode (no effects, metrics only) for 24h, 2) slotting enabled in canary pool (5% traffic) for 48h, 3) ramp to 100% with automatic rollback if cold_p99 > baseline + 10%.

sam: Agreed. I already added simulated-mode to the scheduler. Also added a metric: batch_composition{hot,cold,kernel_family} and cold_wait_time histogram.

devin: One more edge case — short-lived bursts where cold_frac jumps to 100% briefly. The adaptive window should decay quickly to avoid over-allocating slots. Use EWMA with alpha=0.3 for adapt_window_secs.

tom: Also add a hard timeout: if any request hits latency_deadline (e.g., queue_time > 120ms), flush batch immediately. That prevents pathological stalls.

sam: Yup implemented. Flush timeout = min( max_flush_ms_by_tier, dynamic_budget_latency_ms ).

rita: Can you push the canary config + dashboards? I'll coordinate with SRE for canary hosts.

sam: Pushed: `feat/batcher-slotting` PR up. Dashboard panels: cold_p99, cold_wait_time, batch_size_by_kernel_family. Canary config: 5% for realtime customers.

devin: I'll run a model-swap test to ensure kernel selection doesn't regress with slotting on. Also run the 10k synthetic mix test.

sam: Thanks. If this looks good we can ship before Friday. :thumbsup:

tom: :eyes: Great writeup. Keep the bot posted and tag me if cold_p99 creeps.

perf-bot: Canary started at 2026-03-17T15:12:00Z. Monitoring flags: cold_p99, batch_kernel_mismatch_rate, flush_timeout_triggers.
